paragraphs.text: A dramatic river gorge north of Valencia, where towering limestone walls rise above the crystalline Turia River — over 900 routes known for their length, technical vertical faces, and subtle tufa formations.

The medieval village itself, with cobblestone streets winding beneath a 13th-century castle, offers thermal springs and gorge hiking trails for rest days, and a genuinely tranquil counterpoint to the climbing.

practicalCards.body: Fly into Valencia for both arrival and departure. Local transport is organised once you land.

faqs.question: What level do I need to be?
faqs.answer: Previous outdoor sport climbing experience is expected, with a minimum lead grade of indoor 6a or outdoor 5. Suitable for women and men aged 15 and up; physical intensity is medium to high.

faqs.question: Do I need my own gear?
faqs.answer: Bring climbing shoes and a harness you trust. We provide belay devices, helmets, and slings, plus a full kit list once you book (down jacket, headlamp, sleeping bag, approach shoes).

faqs.question: Is food included?
faqs.answer: Food arrangements and any included meals are confirmed before departure.

faqs.question: Can I join this leg without doing Week 1?
faqs.answer: Yes — every leg works as a standalone week. You don't need to have done Sella first, though the technical foundation from Week 1 does help you get more out of Chulilla's longer routes.

faqs.question: What if fewer than 3 people book?
faqs.answer: We need a minimum of 3 participants to run this leg. If numbers don't add up, we'll offer an equivalent (or better) alternative, or a full refund. No hard feelings.

faqs.question: Where do I fly in and out of?
faqs.answer: Valencia Airport, for both arrival and departure.

children.text: North of Valencia, Chulilla's towering walls rise above the crystalline Turia River — over 900 routes known for their length, technical vertical faces, and subtle tufa formations. While Sella introduced you to Spanish limestone, Chulilla is where the trip starts demanding more.

Work iconic sectors like El Balcón, La Muela, and El Oasis, applying Week 1's technical foundation to routes running up to 40 metres on a single pitch — exactly the kind of sustained climbing that forces genuinely efficient movement and strategic resting.
Evenings unfold in a medieval village of cobblestone streets beneath a 13th-century castle, with analysis sessions in local cafés and a rest-day option to soak in nearby thermal springs.

paragraphs.text: A serene valley carved by the Montsant River, home to over 1,600 routes across dozens of sectors on distinctive orange and gray conglomerate — walls punctuated by thousands of pockets of every imaginable size and depth, from gently overhanging to wildly steep caves.

Legendary sectors like Laboratori, Tenebres, and Espadelles draw climbers from around the world, all converging on a tiny, tranquil Catalonian village that feels a world away from anywhere else on the trip.

Margalef is a genuinely different physical puzzle from anything earlier in the trip.

The climbing demands creative thinking, real finger strength, and the confidence to commit to powerful movement between holds that sometimes look more trustworthy than they feel. faqs.answer: Previous outdoor sport climbing experience is expected, with a minimum lead grade of indoor 6a or outdoor 5. Suitable for women and men aged 15 and up; physical intensity is medium to high.

faqs.question: Do I need my own gear?
faqs.answer: Bring climbing shoes and a harness you trust. We provide belay devices, helmets, and slings, plus a full kit list once you book (down jacket, headlamp, sleeping bag, approach shoes).

faqs.question: Is food included?
faqs.answer: Food arrangements and any included meals are confirmed before departure.

faqs.question: What if a leg doesn't reach 3 participants?
faqs.answer: We need a minimum of 3 participants to run any given leg. If numbers don't add up for a specific week, we'll offer an equivalent (or better) alternative, or a full refund for that portion. No hard feelings.

faqs.question: Where do I fly in and out of?
faqs.answer: Fly into Alicante for the start of the trip, and out of Barcelona at the end. If you're only booking individual weeks, each leg has its own nearest airport listed on its page.

Book the whole month below, or use this as your menu — every leg works as a standalone week if four weeks isn't in the cards right now.
No stock photos, no staged sends — just climbers earning it across Spain's four best-known limestone playgrounds.
The crag changes every week; the rhythm doesn't. Maximum climbing time, minimum logistical hassle, wherever you are.
Not sure four weeks is realistic right now? Every leg above works as a standalone week — here's what changes if you go all in.
Ready for the Full España Project?

Starting on the Costa Blanca in Sella, the trip tracks north through Chulilla's dramatic tufa-lined canyon, up to Siurana's legendary technical faces above the Priorat, before finishing in Margalef's otherworldly conglomerate pocket-pulling — roughly 400km of Spain's absolute best limestone.

The itinerary is sequenced for variety as much as geography: from Sella's beginner-friendly diversity through increasingly technical and powerful terrain, so your skills build the same way the trip does.
Shared accommodation in local climbing cottages run by local climbers, at each of the four stops. A private room is possible if arranged ahead, for an extra charge.
Fly into Alicante at the start, out of Barcelona at the end. We're happy to help coordinate shared rental cars within the group between legs.
All safety equipment provided — ropes, draws, helmets, slings. Bring your own shoes and harness if you have preferences; we've got spares if you don't.
Minimum 3 climbers per leg to run. Small enough for real coaching, never a crowd-control exercise, on any single week.
